evidence: Figure 5 presents the corresponding XRD spectra, compared to the commercial Ce0.9Gd0.102_ - (CGO) reference powder diffraction pattern (the powder has been developed by Rhodia in collaboration with B.C.H. Steele, and was used here as reference). A slight decay towards the low diffraction angles for the XRD peaks of the sputtered films can be observed with respect to the reference powder. This could correspond to an increase in the lattice parameter compared to Ceo.9Gdo.lO1.95 , which could be due to an increase of the Gd/Ce ratio. However, chemical analysis showed that Gd/Ce ratio is lower than the target content and optical transmission interferometry curves were typical for a perfectly transparent coating (Fig. 6), i.e. stoichiometric film.
